title: Strengthening Legislation for Crime against Children
what_it_is: Strengthening Legislation for Crime against Children

sections.label: Child pornography law review
sections.summary: The Ministry has started a review on whether new laws, amendments or enhanced punishments on child pornography are needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs whether the Ministry will consider tabling new legislation or amending the Penal Code to introduce specific laws on child pornography.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We have started the review, covering whether existing approaches need to be looked at or whether additional laws need to be put in or whether punishments need to be enhanced.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: It is quite a comprehensive review looking at the situation of minors and we will make an announcement when the review is completed.

sections.label: Review completion and lacuna
sections.summary: The review may find gaps and is expected to be completed before the end of the year.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: And there may be areas where there may be a lacuna as well.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We expect the review to be completed before the end of the year.

sections.label: Stiffer punishments personal view
sections.summary: The speaker's personal view is that punishments need to be stiffened, amid a Penal Code and CPC review.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: My own personal view is that there is certainly a reasonable basis for taking the view that the punishments have to be stiffer.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Speaking personally, I think they need to be stiffened.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Before that we are undertaking a review of the Penal Code and the Criminal Procedure Code (CPC).

sections.label: Public consultation on Penal Code
sections.summary: The speaker intends public consultation for many Penal Code changes, or will explain in Parliament if not done.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: We have started that for some time now.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: I certainly intend that there will be public consultation for many of the Penal Code types of changes that they are thinking of.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: If we do not do it, we will explain in Parliament why.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: But I think it is likely that we will do it.
